name: Centre Ville (Taourirt Kasbah / Avenue Mohammed V)
tagline: The historic and commercial heart of Ouarzazate
description: The town's core, anchored by the earthen Taourirt Kasbah and stretching along Avenue Mohammed V, where most cafes, banks, shops, and budget-to-midrange guesthouses cluster. It is the most walkable part of town and the natural base for a short stay, though it draws the heaviest tourist foot traffic and the occasional vendor hustle near the kasbah entrance.
bestFor: first-time visitors, walkability, easy access to cafes and services
pros: Best concentration of cafes and wifi
cons: Some tourist hustle near the kasbah
Traffic and noise along the main avenue

name: Atlas Film Studios District
tagline: Ouarzazate's Ouallywood, the desert backlot of world cinema
description: Home to the Atlas Corporation Studios and CLA Studios on the town's southwestern edge, where international film and TV productions have long used the surrounding desert as a backdrop. The area mixes studio compounds, film-crew hotels, and open desert terrain, offering a quieter, more spread-out feel than the center, popular with those drawn to the town's cinematic history.
bestFor: film enthusiasts, longer stays wanting space and quiet
pros: Quieter and more spacious than downtown
cons: Further from central cafes and shops
Fewer dining options within walking distance

name: Tabounte / Residential Ouarzazate
tagline: A quieter residential district for longer stays
description: A mostly residential neighborhood east of the center where many locals live, with simpler apartment blocks, small neighborhood shops, and a slower daily rhythm. It offers a more authentic, non-touristic slice of daily Ouarzazate life, at the cost of being a short taxi or walk from the main cafes and sights.
bestFor: longer-term stays, budget rentals, experiencing local life
cons: A taxi or longer walk to central cafes and sights

name: Ait Benhaddou
tagline: The UNESCO-listed ksar just outside town
description: A dramatic fortified earthen ksar about 30 minutes from Ouarzazate, UNESCO-listed and famous as a filming location for numerous major productions. A small cluster of guesthouses sits across the river from the historic ksar, making it possible to stay overnight and see the site at sunrise or sunset once day-trip crowds thin out, with a very small, tranquil village feel.
bestFor: short stays, photography, escaping day-tripper crowds
cons: Crowded with tour groups during midday
